clue.text: Try to get almost completely sightless magical creature

parts.note: to have a go is to try

indicators.note: almost completely says the word is cut short by its final letter

parts.note: sightless means blind

explanation.surface: An instruction to attempt finding a nearly blind fairy-tale creature.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost completely' trims the last letter from BLIND, leaving BLIN.
explanation.definitionFit: A goblin is a small mischievous being of folklore, so it is a magical creature.

clue.text: Live without sex or power

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so the word for live sits around the word for sex

parts.note: to be is to live or exist
IT is an old euphemism for sex or sex appeal

explanation.surface: A choice between a celibate life and one of influence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' means outside here, not lacking. 'or' is just a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Bite means sharpness or force, as in a policy that has real power behind it.

clue.text: Reprimand cat, for example, getting under vehicle

indicators.note: in a down clue, getting under places the animal word below the vehicle word

parts.note: a car is a vehicle
a cat is an example of a pet

explanation.surface: Scolding a cat that has crawled beneath a parked car.
explanation.definitionFit: To carpet someone is British slang for to reprimand them, from being called onto the boss's carpet.

clue.text: Head of restoration raised charge for endangered habitat

indicators.note: head of means the first letter of the next word
in a down clue, raised means the word for charge is read upwards

parts.note: a fee is a charge

explanation.surface: A conservation leader increases a levy to protect a threatened ecosystem.
explanation.walkthrough: 'raised' turns FEE upside down in the column, giving EEF.
explanation.definitionFit: Coral reefs are a well-known example of a threatened habitat.

clue.text: Dodgy period behind the scenes

parts.note: food that is off is dodgy or bad
a stage is a period of development

explanation.surface: A shady stretch of time spent out of public view.
explanation.definitionFit: Offstage describes what happens out of the audience's sight, backstage.

clue.text: Male majority almost left

indicators.note: almost says the word for majority loses its final letter

parts.note: the bulk is the majority

explanation.surface: Most of the men have nearly all gone.
explanation.definitionFit: A bull is the male of cattle and many other large animals.

clue.text: Cable ran broadcast showing hanger-on

indicators.note: broadcast in its sense of scattered, so the letters are spread into a new order

explanation.surface: A cable network aired a programme featuring a sycophant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'broadcast' looks like TV talk alongside 'Cable', but it rearranges CABLE RAN.
explanation.definitionFit: A barnacle clings to ships, so figuratively it is a person who clings on: a hanger-on.

clue.text: Induce companion to hide books one and five

indicators.note: to hide means the word for companion conceals the other pieces inside it

parts.note: a mate is a companion
OT is the Old Testament, a set of books
I is the Roman numeral for one
V is the Roman numeral for five

explanation.surface: Persuading a friend to conceal a couple of library volumes.
explanation.definitionFit: To motivate someone is to induce them to act by giving a reason.

clue.text: Sparing prisoner returning after loud game

indicators.note: after places the prisoner piece behind the loud and game pieces

parts.note: F is forte, the musical direction for loud
RU is rugby union

indicators.note: returning means the word for prisoner is read backwards

parts.note: a lag is a convict, especially an old lag

explanation.surface: A convict coming back after a noisy match is let off lightly.
explanation.definitionFit: Frugal means economical, using things sparingly.

clue.text: Loudly blasted navy perhaps

indicators.note: loudly says the word is spoken, giving one that sounds the same

parts.note: blew means blasted, as a horn or wind does

explanation.surface: Naval guns fired noisily.
explanation.walkthrough: 'navy' reads as the fleet, but it is the dark shade.
explanation.definitionFit: Navy is a dark shade of blue, so it is one example of the colour.

clue.text: Seabirds not featuring in adverts

indicators.note: not featuring says the following word is taken out of the birds

parts.note: puffins are seabirds

explanation.surface: Seabirds missing from commercials.
explanation.definitionFit: Puffs are short promotional pieces praising a product, so they are adverts.

clue.text: Oddly learned nation

indicators.note: oddly means take the first, third, fifth and seventh letters of the following word

explanation.surface: A strangely scholarly country.
explanation.definitionFit: A land can mean a country or nation, as in a foreign land.

clue.text: Bombastic, defiant revolutionary crosses line

indicators.note: crosses means the rearranged letters straddle the abbreviation for line
revolutionary means overturned, so the letters of the word before it are turned into a new order

explanation.surface: A pompous, rebellious agitator steps over the boundary.
explanation.walkthrough: 'revolutionary' makes INFATED; 'crosses' sets L into it after the third letter. 'defiant' looks like part of the definition, but it is the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Inflated language is puffed up and pompous, which is what bombastic means.

clue.text: Compile montage featuring something defective

indicators.note: featuring says the letters are contained within the words that follow

explanation.surface: An editor's instruction to assemble a film montage that includes a flawed shot.
explanation.definitionFit: A lemon is slang for a faulty product, especially a car that keeps breaking down.

clue.text: Set up network attracting European lament

indicators.note: in a down clue, set up means the word for network is read upwards

parts.note: a grid is a network, as in the power grid

explanation.surface: Installing a network that draws in a European grievance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Set up' turns GRID upwards into DIRG; 'attracting' just links E on.
explanation.definitionFit: A dirge is a mournful song for the dead, a lament.

clue.text: A course of action over time becomes offensive

indicators.note: over places the course of action piece next to the time piece

parts.note: a tack is a course of action, from sailing

explanation.surface: A plan which, given time, turns hostile.
explanation.walkthrough: 'offensive' is the noun here, a military assault.
explanation.definitionFit: An offensive is a campaign of attack.

clue.text: Row about German beast

indicators.note: about means the word for row goes around the letter for German

parts.note: a tier is a row, as in theatre seating

explanation.surface: A quarrel concerning a German animal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Row' suggests an argument, but it is a line of seats.
explanation.definitionFit: The tiger is a big cat, a fierce beast.

clue.text: Stop good woman and author returning

parts.note: ST is a saint, a good person, here a woman

indicators.note: returning means the word for the author is read backwards

parts.note: the author of a clue refers to themselves as me

explanation.surface: A virtuous woman halts a writer who is coming back.
explanation.definitionFit: To stem a flow is to stop or check it.

clue.text: Flail about with second husband in the river

indicators.note: in means the pieces before it go inside the following words

parts.note: taken as written
RE means about or concerning

explanation.surface: Someone thrashing about, with a second husband, in the river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flail' is the definition by association: the flail is the tool used for this farm job.
explanation.definitionFit: A thresher beats grain from the husk, just as a flail does; the flail is the threshing tool.

clue.text: Tend to swear without hint of caution after noon

indicators.note: after places the word for swear behind the letter for noon
without says the following letter is taken away from the word for swear

parts.note: to curse is to swear

indicators.note: hint of means just the first letter of the next word

explanation.surface: An instruction to stop cursing so carelessly in the afternoon.
explanation.definitionFit: To nurse a patient is to tend to or care for them.

clue.text: Engineer knew race could be a tie

indicators.note: to engineer is to contrive or rework, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: An engineer was sure the race might end level.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tie' tempts as a dead heat in the race, but it is worn round the neck.
explanation.definitionFit: A necktie is one example of an item worn at the throat.

clue.text: Man covered in, for example, revolting type of butter

indicators.note: covered in means the word for man sits inside the other piece
revolting in its sense of turning over, so the letters are read backwards

parts.note: he refers to a man

explanation.surface: A man smeared in, say, a disgusting kind of butter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'revolting' looks like disgust, but it signals turning over, giving GE.
explanation.definitionFit: Ghee is clarified butter used in South Asian cooking.

clue.text: Wry, smooth and in charge

parts.note: to iron is to smooth

explanation.surface: Someone dry-humoured, polished and in control.
explanation.definitionFit: Ironic humour is wry, saying the opposite of what is meant.

clue.text: Imposed target involving uniformed group

indicators.note: involving means the word for target wraps around the other piece

parts.note: an end is an aim or target
the police force is a uniformed group

explanation.surface: A quota forced on the police.
explanation.definitionFit: Something enforced is imposed by authority.

clue.text: Vicious fellow replacing head of drill

indicators.note: replacing head of means the abbreviation takes the place of the first letter of the next word

parts.note: to pierce is to drill through

explanation.surface: A nasty man taking over at the front of a drill session.
explanation.walkthrough: F replaces the P at the front of PIERCE.
explanation.definitionFit: Fierce means savage or vicious, as a fierce dog.

clue.text: Influenced by old institute being cast out

parts.note: EX means former or old
led means guided or influenced

explanation.surface: Someone swayed by a former college who ends up banished.
explanation.definitionFit: Exiled people are banished, cast out from their homeland.

clue.text: Lives with the French somewhere surrounded by water

parts.note: is means lives or exists
LE is French for the

explanation.surface: Living with the French people on an island.
explanation.definitionFit: An isle is an island, land with water all around it.

clue.text: Throw out unusual item

indicators.note: unusual means the letters of the next word are in an odd order

explanation.surface: Discard a strange object.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Throw out' suggests discarding, but means giving off, like heat or light.
explanation.definitionFit: To emit is to give off or send forth, as a lamp emits light.

clue.text: Wide, robust creature

parts.note: W is the abbreviation for wide, as in cricket
hale means robust and healthy

explanation.surface: A broad, sturdy animal.
explanation.definitionFit: A whale is a sea mammal, one kind of creature.

clue.text: A room with unknown host

parts.note: Y is an algebraic unknown

explanation.surface: A spare room with a mysterious person hosting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'host' suggests a party giver, but means a great multitude.
explanation.definitionFit: A host is an army or large crowd, as in the heavenly host.

clue.text: Hide second family

parts.note: kin means family

explanation.surface: Conceal a second family.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hide' reads as a verb, but is the noun: an animal's pelt.
explanation.definitionFit: A hide is an animal's skin.

clue.text: Observed shark eating elongated needlefish heads

indicators.note: heads means the first letters of the words before it

explanation.surface: A shark was watched devouring the heads of long thin fish.
explanation.definitionFit: Seen and observed both mean noticed with the eyes.

clue.text: Part of eye engineers can advance

parts.note: RE is the Royal Engineers, a British Army corps
a tin is a can
A is an abbreviation for advance

explanation.surface: Engineers might make progress on the anatomy of the eye.
explanation.definitionFit: The retina is the light-sensitive layer at the back of the eyeball.

clue.text: Cram leek roughly into fish

indicators.note: roughly means the letters are rearranged in a rough, approximate order

explanation.surface: Stuff chopped leeks into a fish as a rough stuffing.
explanation.definitionFit: Mackerel is an oily sea fish.
